Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Tafsir of Surat al-Taghabun

It is Madinan according to the majority of scholars. Al-Dahhak said: it is Makki. Al-Kalbi said: it is both Makki and Madani. Its meaning is that some of it is Makki and some of it is Madani. And Allah knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah; to Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent.﴾ We have already mentioned the meanings of this before.

The Qur'an, 64:2: "It is He who created you, and among you is the disbeliever and among you is the believer."

Ali ibn Abi Talha al-Walibi said: "He created you as disbelievers and created you as believers." This was said by Ibn Abbas. This meaning is supported by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah, and a master, and chaste﴾. He thus informs that Allah the Exalted created him so.

There is a report that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted created Yahya as one blessed (sa'id) in his mother's womb, and created Pharaoh as a disbeliever in his mother's womb."

Sufyan narrated from Amr ibn Dinar, from [Abu] al-Tufayl, who said: "I heard Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, say: 'The wretched one is he who was made wretched in his mother's womb, and the blessed one is he who takes admonition from others.'" I said: "May the mother of the wretched one be bereaved, before he has done any deed!" Then I met Hudhayfah ibn Asid, whose kunya was Abu Shurayhah al-Ghifari, and I mentioned that to him. He said: "Shall I not inform you of something more astonishing than this! I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'When the drop (nutfah) settles in the womb of the woman for forty nights, or he said: forty-five nights, an angel enters upon her and says: "O Lord, is he wretched or blessed?" Allah decides, and the angel writes. Then he says: "Is it male or female?" Allah decides, and the angel writes. Then he says: "O Lord, what is his term? What is his deed? What is his provision? What is his misfortune?" Allah the Exalted decrees, and the angel writes. Then he rolls up the scroll, and nothing is added to it or subtracted from it until the Day of Resurrection.'"

Sufyan also narrated from Talhah ibn Yahya, from his paternal aunt, from Aishah bint Talhah, from Aishah, Mother of the Believers, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a child from the Ansar to pray over. I said: "Happy (Tuba) for him! A sparrow of the sparrows of Paradise!" He said: "Or otherwise, O Aishah. Indeed Allah the Exalted created Paradise and created for it people, whom He created for it while they were in their fathers' loins, and He created the Fire and created for it people, while they were in their fathers' loins."

He (al-Samani), may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu Ali al-Shafi'i in Mecca informed us of these two hadiths: Abu al-Hasan ibn Firas informed us, al-Dibli informed us, Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi informed us, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah... the report as we have mentioned.

The second opinion regarding the verse is that its meaning is: "Among you is the disbeliever, [who disbelieves] in the fact that Allah created him, and among you is the believer, and among you is the wicked one." The well-known view is the first opinion.

As for His words: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, it is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 3:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, meaning: with justice. It is also said: with perfect craftsmanship and good (taqdir, measure). It is also said: for the truth.

His words: ﴿and He shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾. Muqatil said: He created Adam with His own hand, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿and He shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾. From others: it has the meaning of His words, may He be exalted: {Certainly We created man in the best of stature}. From some of them: He said, "He created man in the best form, and if Allah had presented the forms to him, he would not have chosen any form other than his own."

His words: ﴿and to Him is the final return﴾, meaning: the place of return.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah is All-Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾. That is, of what the breasts conceal.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before?﴾ This is an address to the polytheists of Quraysh.

And His saying: ﴿So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾ i.e., in this world.

And His saying: ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ i.e., in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 6:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning: with manifest evidences.

And His saying: ﴿So they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?"﴾ is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾.

And His saying: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away﴾, meaning: they denied and turned away.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah dispensed [with them]﴾, meaning: Allah is free of need for their obedience, their worship, and their affirmation of His oneness.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾, meaning: He is independent of the actions of the servants, and He is praised by His creatures for the blessings He bestows upon them. It is also said: "Ḥamīd" means worthy of praise (mustaḥaqq lil-ḥamd). It is also said: "Ḥamīd" means one who loves to be praised (yuḥibb an yuḥmad). And it has been established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no one more zealous (aghyar) than Allah, and no one loves praise more than Allah, and no one loves excuses more than Allah."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 7:

And His Exalted saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim﴾. It is related from Mujahid that he disliked the word *za'amū* (زعموا), and likewise it is related from Ibn Mas'ud. In some of the tafsirs (works of Qur'anic exegesis) it is related from Ibn 'Umar that he said: "It is the kunya (agnomen) of lying." A similar view is related from Shurayh. Here, *fa-za'amū* (فزعموا) carries the sense of *qālū* (قالوا, "they said") and *akhbarū* (أخبروا, "they informed"). The poet said:

*Did Sabasa not claim today that I have grown old, and that men like me no longer keep secrets well?*

And His saying: ﴿that they will never be resurrected﴾, meaning: after death.

And His saying: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected﴾. His saying *balā* (بلى, "yes") in this place is to contradict the people in what they claimed. It is like the statement of one who says to another: "I had ordered you to do such-and-such," and the man replies: "I did not hear, and you did not order me to do it," so he says: "Yes," meaning: "You are lying; you did hear, and I did order you."

And His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be informed of what you did, and that is easy for Allah﴾, meaning: easy.

Almost-verbatim translation:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, and the light which We have sent down﴾, meaning: the Qur'an which We have sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, meaning: Knowing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 9:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾ meaning: the Day of Resurrection. It is called the Day of Gathering because on it the first and the last (generations) are gathered, and the people of the heavens and the people of the earth are gathered together.

And His words: ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain (al-taghabun)﴾. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: it is a name for the Day of Resurrection. Regarding taghabun there are two meanings. The first: the people of truth defraud the people of falsehood, and the people of faith defraud the people of disbelief.

The second view: God, exalted is He, designated for every one of His creatures a place in the Fire and a place in the Paradise. So whoever was a believer inherits the place of the disbeliever in Paradise, and whoever was a disbeliever inherits the place of the believer in the Fire. This is the meaning of taghabun on the Day of Resurrection. It is also reported from some scholars that ghabn (loss/defrauding) is taking a thing for less than its value. Through the disparity that occurs between the value and what is less than it, taghabun arises. Thus the believers, since they worked for Paradise and lasting bliss, have defrauded the people of the Fire, while the disbelievers, since they preferred transient bliss over lasting bliss, and the abode that perishes over the abode that does not perish, have been defrauded. Zayd ibn 'Ali said: they defrauded themselves. Here ghabn means loss, and in (other) passages it has this meaning.

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph﴾. Its meaning is clear.

God the Exalted says: ﴿Those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever. And wretched is the destination.﴾ That is, the return and the place to which one turns.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 11:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning: by His knowledge, His decree and His determination.

And His words: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart﴾. ʿAlqamah said: "Whoever believes in Allah during calamity," meaning: he knows that it is from Allah, and He guides his heart to istirjaʿ (saying "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return") and to submission to the command of Allah, exalted is He. Similar is related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr. And from some of them: "He guides his heart," meaning: to patience when tested, to gratitude when blessed, and to forgiveness when wronged. ʿIkrimah said: "He guides his heart to certainty, so he knows that what missed him would never have struck him, and that what struck him would never have missed him." Al-Azhari mentioned in his book that the meaning of His words ﴿He guides his heart﴾ is: He makes it guided. This view is supported by what is related from Ibn Jurayj, that he said: "Whoever knows Allah has a heart that is guided."

And His words: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾.
His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then the duty of Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾ That is: the clear.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him; so let the believers rely upon Allah.﴾ We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 64, verse 14:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾. That is: enemies to you, so beware of them. Ibn 'Abbas said: The verse was revealed concerning a people who had embraced Islam in Makkah and wished to emigrate to Madinah, but their children and their wives prevented them, saying: "You have left us for your religion, so do not leave us for your own selves." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. And it is related from Mujahid, who said: The verse was revealed concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who had suffered harshness from his family and his children.

And His saying: ﴿And if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: When these people remained behind because of their families and then emigrated afterwards, and they saw people of their own tribe who had embraced Islam and had preceded them in emigration and had gained understanding of the religion, they grieved over that with intense grief, and they intended to punish their families and children and to withhold spending on them. So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿And if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, meaning: a tribulation and a test. The meaning of the tribulation and the test in regard to wealth and children is that a person becomes occupied with them and turns away from obedience to God, and the pursuit of wealth and the pleasure of children drive him to disobey God. In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is related that he said: "Children make one miserly, cowardly, sorrowful and ignorant." Its meaning is that they drive one to stinginess, cowardice, grief and ignorance. And from Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, it is related that he said: Whoever takes a wife, wealth and a child has become a slave to the world.

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Buraydah related, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering a sermon when al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, entered, wearing two red shirts and stumbling in them. So the Prophet (ﷺ) descended from the pulpit, carried them, placed them before himself, then recited His saying: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾. Then he said: "I saw these two boys stumbling in their shirts, and I could not restrain myself until I came down and carried them."

And they recited, regarding the word fitnah (trial), a line of poetry by one of them:

(The people have been tried in their religion... and Ibn ʿUthman has left behind a long evil.)

Meaning: the people have been afflicted.

And His saying: ﴿And with God is a great reward﴾, meaning: a abundant one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 16:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. Rabi' ibn Anas said: "With your effort and your capacity." Ma'mar narrated from Qatadah that this verse abrogated His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾. A similar view is reported from a group of the Successors (tabi'un). A group of the people of knowledge said: "The better position is to say that this verse is a concession (rukhsah) and is not abrogating (nasikhah)." Al-Qaffal mentioned that this verse clarifies His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾, because Allah, the Exalted, does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. He mentioned something similar from Ibn 'Isa and others.

The preferred view is that held by the early generations (al-salaf), and it is the first opinion. We have already mentioned from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾, that it means: He is obeyed and not disobeyed, He is remembered and not forgotten, and He is thanked and not ungrateful.

His saying: ﴿And listen, and obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves﴾. The word ﴿better﴾ (khayran) is in the accusative because of an implied verb: "Be mindful of Allah in spending, [spend] what is better." A similar example is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Cease, it is better for you﴾.

His saying: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul﴾, meaning: from the miserliness of his soul. It is said: stinginess (shuh) is the withholding of the obligatory rights of Allah. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Stinginess here is injustice rather than miserliness, because Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿And whoever is miserly, he is only miserly against his own soul﴾."

His saying: ﴿Those are the successful﴾. We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It is spending in the way of Allah. And it is said: it is all the rights of wealth, and it was called a loan because Allah, exalted is He, rewards them for it and gives them its recompense, so it is in the position of a loan.

There is a third view on it: that the lending here is the saying of the one who says: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-Hamdu li-Allah (Praise be to Allah), La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), and Allah is greatest (Allahu akbar). Al-Qaffal mentioned that some of the early generations (al-salaf), when they heard a beggar say: "Who will lend Allah a goodly loan?", would say: Subhan Allah, al-Hamdu li-Allah, La ilaha illa Allah, and Allah is greatest. As for His saying ﴿goodly﴾, it means: good, with your souls content with it. And it is said: from the best of wealth, not from its worst.

His saying ﴿He will multiply it for you﴾ means: He makes one become ten. And it is said: it is multiplied without reference to a known number.

His saying ﴿and forgive you, and Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing﴾: Gratitude (shukr) from Allah is His recompense to the good-doers, the recompense of one who thanks them for their good deeds. And it is said: gratitude from Allah is pardoning evil deeds and accepting good deeds. And it is said: it is pardoning much and accepting little.

His saying ﴿Forbearing (halim)﴾ means: granting the servants respite and not hastening to punish them.
His words, exalted is He: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Wise﴾. Its meaning is apparent.
